codes.sample: 390 management undergraduates at selected state universities in Sri Lanka; cross-sectional survey (p. 12: "A total of 390 valid responses were obtained and used for analysis")
codes.ai_system: AI tools in general (ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, Gemini, Notion AI)
codes.dependence_measures: AI Over-Reliance scale: 12 items, 5-point Likert, α = 0.876, ad hoc. It has 4 dimensions: dependency on AI tools (includes "inability to complete tasks without AI"), reduced critical thinking, excessive trust in AI, and decline in independent learning (pp. 10, 13).
codes.possible_duplicate: None identified.
codes.note: The only outcome is academic productivity (8 items), which is not an eligible correlate. The one correlation is AI over-reliance with academic productivity, r = -.658 (Table 3, p. 14). Data are internally inconsistent: r = -.658 but R = .642 and β = -.642, and F = 72.31 does not match t = -16.50. Planned n was 150–300, but 390 were reported. This is a credibility concern.

codes.sample: Convenience sample of N=33 users recruited through public outreach channels who completed the online PAUSI. No demographics reported (p. 17).
codes.ai_system: AI in general: LLMs and conversational AI ("talking to AI")
codes.dependence_measures: The Problem AI Use Severity Index (PAUSI) has 10 items scored 0–3, for a total of 0–27. It is adapted from the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI). Scores fall into four categories: 0, 1–2, 3–8 and 9 or more ("Problem AI use"). Items are listed in Appendix A.
codes.possible_duplicate: None identified. A future longitudinal validation study of the PAUSI that includes the SWEMWBS may report on an overlapping sample.
codes.note: The PAUSI is a dependence measure, and the report gives preliminary descriptive results (23 of 33 respondents, about 70%, scored 9 or more). However, no correlate was measured. The SWEMWBS (well-being) is only proposed as a Time 2 outcome for a future study (pp. 13, 22). "Escape negative feelings" (Q6) is a PAUSI item, not a separate measure. Much of the report is theoretical or advocacy content.

codes.sample: 102 Polish primary and secondary school teachers (80 women, 20 men, 2 undisclosed) from Warsaw's Bielany district who use AI chatbots. They come from 136 consenting participants in a prevention project; online survey, Nov–Dec 2025.
codes.ai_system: AI chatbots in general (LLM-based, e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot)
codes.dependence_measures: An author-developed 3-item Problematic AI Use index based on ICD-11 behavioural addiction criteria (life-balance disruption, use beyond intention, continued use despite harm), 5-point scale, α = .685, summed/mean index (Appendix 2).

correlations.correlate: Anxiety and depressive symptoms (combined; psychological distress)

codes.possible_duplicate: None identified. The sample is part of a broader prevention project ("Bielany promotes prevention, counters addiction, and supports diversity"), so other reports from the same project may exist.
codes.note: PHQ-4 is reported only as a combined anxiety + depression total, with no separate subscale correlations; code it as psychological distress or combined anxiety/depression. The escape motive was a single item reported descriptively, with no correlation with problematic use. Mediation betas (Table 3) are multivariable and were not used. Correlations with time of use are not eligible correlates.

codes.sample: Not reported in the retrieved text. The text has no methods or participants section.
codes.ai_system: Unknown. Presumably AI tools in general (TOT_AID may stand for AI dependence), but the text does not define it.
codes.dependence_measures: Possibly TOT_AID (presumably 'AI dependence'), used as a second mediator in serial moderated mediation models (TOT_X → TOT_PE → TOT_AID → TOT_AA, moderated by TOT_MO). No variable labels, instrument names or item details are given, so it cannot be confirmed as an AI-dependence scale.
codes.possible_duplicate: This looks like a supplementary file (SEM output) for a main manuscript of the same title on OSF. The main paper should be retrieved and checked as the same report or sample.
codes.note: The retrieved text has only mediation tables for Models 1–7 (predictors NF, AES, NAE, SC, FD, SN, AS; mediators PE and AID; moderator MO; outcome AA), and the abbreviations are not defined. SC/AS might be self-control or academic stress. There is no correlation matrix; only path, indirect and total effects are given (not eligible under I4). The main text and methods are needed.

codes.sample: Study 3: 290 US adult AI users recruited on Prolific (age 20–78, M = 42.30; 50.69% female). Studies 2 (N = 300, US) and 4 (N = 122, Singapore) used only the AI Fatigue Scale.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI / AI tools in general (AI used in daily life)
codes.dependence_measures: Generative AI Dependency Scale (Goh et al., 2025), 11 items, 5-point scale. Subscales: cognitive preoccupation, negative consequences, withdrawal. Total α = .93 (Study 3 only). The focal construct, AI fatigue, is not a dependence measure.
codes.possible_duplicate: The GAIDS comes from Goh, Hartanto & Majeed (2025, CHB Reports) and is used here by the same lab, but this appears to be a separate Study 3 Prolific sample. It may overlap with other Hartanto-lab samples (e.g., AI Attachment Scale, Critical Thinking in AI Use Scale).
codes.note: GAIDS is correlated only with latent AI fatigue (r = .11, p. 38). Eligible correlates (neuroticism and other Big Five, fear of AI, affect) are correlated only with AI fatigue. Correlations among other variables are not reported, and no table links GAIDS to an eligible correlate. Data are promised on ResearchBox.

codes.sample: 1,750 teachers (kindergarten to high school) in one Chinese city who use generative AI. Online survey, 15 Jan to 10 Feb 2025. The text is inconsistent on gender: it says 85.57% male, but Table 2 gives 1,480 female and 270 male.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI tools / LLM chatbots in general (DeepSeek 64%, ERNIE Bot 48.9%, 360 Zhinao, ChatGPT, Claude and others)
codes.dependence_measures: Generative AI Addiction (GA), 4 items adapted from Hu et al. (2023), e.g. "I have tried to limit my use of generative AI tools, but I find it difficult to do so". 5-point Likert scale; α=0.93, CR=0.93, AVE=0.77.

correlations.correlate: Mood regulation via AI (possible coping motive; AI-specific)
correlations.correlate_instrument: Mood Regulation, 3 items (Hutchison & Gunthert, 2013), e.g. using GenAI to reduce stress

correlations.quote: Table 4. Correlation matrix ... GA row: -0.65 (SE column)

codes.possible_duplicate: None identified. The author (Yiran Du) has published other generative-AI survey studies; check for overlap with other Chinese teacher samples collected in early 2025.
codes.note: Borderline: valid AI-addiction scale, but all correlates are AI-specific. Self-efficacy is AI-use self-efficacy (probably not eligible). Mood regulation (AI to relieve stress) might count as a coping motive. Table 4 latent correlations with GA are all strongly negative (PA -0.92), though SEM paths are positive and |r| exceeds √AVE, so they are suspect.

codes.sample: Six studies, N=1333 in total (Singapore university students and US adults). Correlates come from Study 5 (N=131 Singapore university students; Big Five) and Study 6 (US adults from CloudResearch Connect who had used generative AI at least once; N=261 in the Method, N=266 in Fig. 4 and Table 8).
codes.ai_system: Generative AI in general (ChatGPT, Replika, DALL-E and other tools)
codes.dependence_measures: Generative AI Dependency Scale (new; 11 items rated 1–5). It has three subscales: cognitive preoccupation, negative consequences and withdrawal, under a higher-order dependency factor. Study 5 also used the 3-item Generative AI Addiction scale (Zhou & Zhang, 2024), but only for convergent validity (r=.85 with dependency).

correlations.quote: It was positively associated with FoMO to a medium extent (r = .21, p = .001).
Generative AI dependency was positively correlated with procrastination to a small extent (r = .16, p = .015)
A small positive correlation was also observed with loneliness (r = .15, p = .025).

correlations.correlate_instrument: Self-Views scale (Majeed et al., 2023), self-esteem items
correlations.quote: No significant associations were found with self-esteem (r = −.09, p = .174)
dependency was positively associated with life satisfaction to a medium extent (r = .25, p < .001)
exceeded all |r| values between Generative AI Dependency Scale and the Big Five domains (... Neuroticism: .67 > .16

codes.possible_duplicate: This is the PsyArXiv preprint of Goh, Hartanto & Majeed (2025), Computers in Human Behavior Reports, 100845 (doi:10.1016/j.chbr.2025.100845), so the two report the same samples. The Study 4–6 data were also pooled for the invariance tests.
codes.note: All values are latent CFA correlations (standardized covariances). The observed zero-order matrices are in the ResearchBox #3834 supplement (AM 11, 13), not retrieved. Study 6 N: 261 in Method, 266 in Fig. 4/Table 8. Big Five values are printed as |r| only; their signs are only in Fig. 3. Negative affect was not coded as an eligible correlate.

codes.sample: Study 2: 780 Chinese adults recruited via Credamo (65.6% female, aged 19–62, M = 30.75). Study 1 samples (N = 500; N = 896) did not measure AI addiction.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI in general (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini named as examples)
codes.dependence_measures: AI addiction (AIA): a 3-item unidimensional Generative AI addiction scale (Cao et al., 2020; Zhou & Zhang, 2024), e.g. "I feel a bit uneasy when I cannot use generative AI". Rated on a 7-point scale, α = .68.

correlations.correlate: Negative attitudes toward AI (GAAIN): a possible proxy for AI-related anxiety/fear of AI
correlations.correlate_instrument: Chinese short GAAIS, negative subscale (6 items, e.g. 'I think AI is dangerous')
correlations.quote: GAAIN was positively associated with AIA (r = .41, p < .001)

correlations.correlate: Positive sense of agency (SoPA): borderline, not clearly self-control
correlations.correlate_instrument: Chinese Sense of Agency Scale (Tapal et al., 2017), SoPA subscale
correlations.quote: SoPA (r = -.33, p < .001) and SoNA (r = .33, p < .001) negatively and positively related to AIA

correlations.correlate_instrument: Chinese Sense of Agency Scale (Tapal et al., 2017), SoNA subscale
correlations.quote: SoPA (r = -.33, p < .001) and SoNA (r = .33, p < .001) negatively and positively related to AIA

codes.possible_duplicate: None identified.
codes.note: Valid AI-addiction measure with zero-order correlations (Table 3). But no listed correlate is clearly measured: only attitudes toward AI (GAAIS) and sense of agency. GAAIN items (discomfort, danger, AI 'sinister') overlap with fear of AI. If accepted as AI-related anxiety: eligible (r = .41). Otherwise: not eligible (no_eligible_correlate).

codes.sample: 5,855 Chinese adolescents with complete AIED data, out of 6,361 recruited, aged 13–17 per Methods (observed range 11–21), from 7 middle and high schools in 5 provinces of Mainland China. This is wave 1 (April 2025) of a three-wave longitudinal study. The sample was randomly split into an EFA subsample (n=2,927) and a CFA subsample (n=2,928).
codes.ai_system: AI chatbots / LLM chatbots in general (e.g., ChatGPT)
codes.dependence_measures: AI Chatbot Emotional Dependence (AIED) Scale: 5 items, 7-point scale, α=.89, newly developed here. AI Chatbot Dependence Scale (X. Zhang et al., 2025): 8 items, 7-point scale, α=.93. The two correlate at r(5853)=.67.
codes.possible_duplicate: Wave 1 of a three-wave longitudinal adolescent dataset (Wei, Liu, Cheung; HKU). Other papers from the same cohort may report AIED or AI chatbot dependence alongside psychological correlates. Check for overlapping samples.
codes.note: Scale validation paper. Apart from the two dependence scales, only age, sex and educational stage were measured. Loneliness, social anxiety, depression and attachment anxiety are named only as future research topics. The only r reported (.67) links two dependence scales, so it is not an eligible correlate.

codes.sample: Planned: about 400-500 adults (18+) per site. In Germany, the general population via Bilendi GmbH; in Italy, recruited through university channels and online platforms. No data collected yet: "Data does not yet exist."
codes.ai_system: Large Language Models / AI companions
codes.dependence_measures: Planned measure: the LLM-Dependency Scale (LLM-D12; German version by Liebherr et al., accepted), covering instrumental vs. relational dependency. Also planned: EHARS (emotional attachment to AI) and an AI Companion Scale. The Italian versions are back-translated.
codes.possible_duplicate: Look for a later results paper from this preregistration (OSF jzwfq; German and Italian samples; attachment style, LLM-D12, loneliness, DERS). That paper would probably be eligible because it plans to correlate LLM dependency with attachment anxiety/avoidance and loneliness.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration, so it is a protocol without results: "Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists." The planned exposure (LLM-D12) and correlates (attachment anxiety/avoidance, loneliness) would qualify, but no correlations are reported.

codes.sample: Planned N = 250-300 (AI companion users, mostly young users); no data collected at registration ("78-2: No, no data have been collected for this study yet").
codes.ai_system: AI companions
codes.dependence_measures: Planned: Emotional Dependence Towards AI (the DV, "78-9: Emotional Dependence Towards AI"). The instrument is not named.
codes.possible_duplicate: A later results paper or thesis from this preregistration (OSF b28gp) may exist and could be eligible, since emotional loneliness and emotional dependence on AI companions are the planned measures. Check for one.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (AsPredicted template) with no results. The registration says no data had been collected. The planned analysis is Hayes PROCESS Model 14. There are no reported associations, so it counts as a protocol without results.

codes.sample: Planned: N = 400 adult users (18+) of generative AI chatbots, recruited from a Polish internet research panel; three waves at 3-month intervals. The registration says "Data does not yet exist."
codes.ai_system: Generative AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini)
codes.dependence_measures: Planned: a modified Bergen Facebook Addiction Scale (Polish adaptation), with "Facebook" replaced by "AI chatbots" (6 addiction symptoms), following Yao et al. (2025).
codes.possible_duplicate: A future results paper from OSF registration 87xq5 (loneliness, social and general self-efficacy, and problematic AI chatbot use; RI-CLPM, Polish sample) would report the eligible data.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (protocol) with no results ("No part of the data ... exists"). The planned measures would be eligible: a BFAS-adapted dependence scale, plus loneliness (R-UCLA) and general self-efficacy. Look for the later results publication.

codes.sample: Planned: school-enrolled Chinese adolescents aged 12–18. Target baseline cohort is about 800–1,000; the primary analysis uses consistent generative-AI users. Three waves from T1 (October 2026). No data collected yet.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI / LLMs (general)
codes.dependence_measures: LLM-D12 (LLM Dependence Scale), planned as two six-item subscale means: instrumental dependency (ID) and relational/emotional dependency (RD). No total score.
codes.possible_duplicate: A later results paper from this cohort (OSF w2hq3) could become eligible. Check for it.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (protocol) and has no results. Item 344-4 says: "Data does not yet exist." The planned correlates are WHO-5 well-being, single-item loneliness and PHQ-4 psychological distress (anxiety/depression), but no associations are reported yet.

codes.sample: Planned: Chinese participants recruited from a Chinese online platform. Target N = 150 (75 per group), up to 200 to be recruited. Between-subjects randomized experiment on self-threat delivered through AI-rated feedback.
codes.ai_system: AI in general (AI rating system used in the manipulation; AI dependency measured with the DIA scale)
codes.dependence_measures: Planned: "AI dependency: 5-point Scale for Dependence on Artificial Intelligence (DIA; Morales-García et al., 2024)", given at baseline and after priming.
codes.possible_duplicate: A later results paper or dataset from this preregistration (OSF s8h2f) may report the planned correlations. If one turns up, it should be screened separately.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (a protocol) with no results. It plans to measure AI dependency (DIA) alongside eligible correlates: self-esteem (RSES), state anxiety (STAI), life satisfaction (SWLS) and AI anxiety (AIAS). It also plans correlation analyses of the baseline measures, but no data or coefficients are reported. Excluded as a protocol without results.

codes.sample: Planned: N=500 German-speaking adults aged 18-35 in Germany/Austria/Switzerland who use ChatGPT for health questions (~167 per country). No data collected yet.
codes.ai_system: ChatGPT (health-related use)
codes.dependence_measures: Problematic ChatGPT Use Scale (PCUS; Yu et al., 2024), 11 items, 4-point scale, sum score. Planned measure only.
codes.possible_duplicate: The future results paper from the Chat-Health project (Ruhr-University Bochum / Medical University of Vienna / University of Zurich) would use the planned sample from this preregistration.
codes.note: OSF preregistration (u57ws) with no results: "Data does not yet exist." Planned correlates are only single-item self-rated mental/physical health and stress/distress (1-10) and suicide items. Most planned analyses are multivariable regressions. Check for the later results report.

codes.sample: Planned: about 1000 university students (undergraduate, postgraduate, PhD) across China, online survey ("We estimates 1000 participants"). At registration, data collection was still ongoing and no data had been looked at.
codes.ai_system: ChatGPT (used for academic help)
codes.dependence_measures: Planned: a 6-item ChatGPT dependency scale adapted from Hu et al. (2023) and Zhang et al. (2024), rated on a 5-point Likert scale. Planned correlates: neuroticism (NEO-FFI), impulsivity (BIS-15), self-critical perfectionism, needs frustration and negative academic emotions (AEQ-S, which includes anxiety).
codes.possible_duplicate: This is OSF preregistration 4ursz (2024-06-05). The results may have been published later as a separate article on the same sample (ChatGPT dependency, neuroticism, impulsivity, needs frustration, I-PACE, Chinese students). That later report should be assessed.
codes.note: This is a preregistration with no results. It plans descriptive statistics and inter-correlations, but none are reported because data collection was still ongoing. The design would otherwise be relevant: it has an eligible dependence scale and eligible correlates (neuroticism, impulsivity, anxiety within negative academic emotions). It is worth searching for the published results.

codes.sample: Planned only. A three-wave cohort of school-enrolled Chinese adolescents aged 12–18 in one region, with a target baseline N of about 800–1,000. The analytic sample is limited to consistent AI users (consistent_ai_user=1). T1 is planned for October 2026, and the text states "Data does not yet exist."
codes.ai_system: Generative AI / LLMs in general
codes.dependence_measures: LLM-D12, split into two six-item subscale means: instrumental AI dependency (ID) and relational/emotional AI dependency (RD).
codes.possible_duplicate: The future results paper from this preregistration (OSF hcq69) will report the same cohort. Other preregistrations or papers under ethics approvals Z2026SY016/Z2026SY017 (Capital Medical University) that use the LLM-D12 may share the same sample.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (protocol) with no results. The text says data collection has not begun. Correlates are planned (WHO-5 well-being, loneliness, PHQ-4 distress), but no data are reported, so the record is excluded as a protocol without results. Also, the planned analysis uses panel GVAR partial networks, not zero-order associations. Check for the future results paper.

codes.sample: Planned: school-enrolled Chinese adolescents aged 12–18 at baseline, target n ≈ 800–1,000, three-wave cohort (T1 October 2026). Data do not exist yet ("Data does not yet exist").
codes.ai_system: Generative AI / LLMs in general (LLM-D12)
codes.dependence_measures: LLM-D12, with separate six-item instrumental dependency (ID) and relational/emotional dependency (RD) means; planned, not yet given to anyone
codes.possible_duplicate: Future result papers from OSF registration qw6gh (Capital Medical University, ethics Z2026SY017) may meet the criteria once published.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (a protocol) and has no results. Section 344-4 says "Data does not yet exist", and 344-14 says T1 data collection has not begun. Planned correlates include PHQ-4 (depression/anxiety), WHO-5 (well-being) and loneliness, so check for the outcome paper later.

codes.sample: Planned: UK-based Prolific participants aged 18–70, 1:1 female:male, 110 per treatment group (power analysis). The registration states that no data had been collected yet.
codes.ai_system: LLMs giving recommendations and reasoning on MMLU-Pro multiple-choice questions (one, two or three models)
codes.dependence_measures: None self-reported. Overreliance is a behavioural task outcome: 'the proportion of times participants updated their answer to match the AI recommendation, conditioned on the AI recommendation not being correct'.
codes.possible_duplicate: Any later results paper from this experiment (OSF registration nrmke) would describe the same planned sample.
codes.note: OSF/AsPredicted preregistration with no results ('No, no data have been collected for this study yet'), so E5_design is the first reason that applies. It would also fail E1, because overreliance is measured only as behaviour in an experimental task, and no eligible psychological correlate is planned.

codes.sample: Planned: at least 351 participants recruited via Sona (Spring 2026). No data collected yet ("78-2: No, no data have been collected for this study yet.").
codes.ai_system: Custom-built conversational AI chatbots (Reassurer vs. Challenger)
codes.dependence_measures: None registered for Study 2. The registered outcomes are motivation to seek reassurance from AI, a tuning-credit allocation task, coded chat transcripts, attitudes toward the AI and future use intentions. AI dependence comes up only as a project-level outcome (Study 1), and no instrument is named for it.
codes.possible_duplicate: This registration is for Study 2 of the 'Me, Myself, and AI' project. Study 1, which may have measured AI dependence, may have its own registration or a later publication. Screen any such report separately.
codes.note: This is a preregistration (AsPredicted template on OSF) with no results; no data have been collected. Study 2 also has no registered measure of AI dependence, and none of the eligible correlates is listed (existential isolation is not one of them). Check whether a Study 1 report or a later results paper exists.

codes.sample: Planned: target 244 adults (18+), convenience sample recruited via University of Amsterdam (subject pool, flyers), public spaces, social media and personal networks. No data collected at registration ("Data does not yet exist").
codes.ai_system: Generative AI in general (developmental AI use)
codes.dependence_measures: Generative AI Dependency Scale (Goh et al., 2025), 11 items, 5-point Likert, scored as the unweighted mean (planned).
codes.possible_duplicate: A later thesis or article reporting results of this preregistered UvA study (OSF tpnd4) may exist and should be screened on its own.
codes.note: OSF preregistration with no results ("Data does not yet exist"), so a protocol without results. Planned correlates (need satisfaction: autonomy, competence, relatedness; network characteristics) are not clearly on the eligible list. Analyses are mainly moderation regressions, though a descriptive correlation matrix is mentioned.

codes.sample: Planned only: about 800 UK (England) adolescents aged 13-18 who use AI chatbots, recruited through schools (at least 15 schools/sites where feasible). No data are reported; data collection had started but the authors had not looked at the data.
codes.ai_system: AI chatbots in general (the participant's primary chatbot), rated in a randomly assigned context: school/work use or non-school/private use
codes.dependence_measures: A context-specific "AI Dependency" block, scored as a mean. The scale is not named or described in this text; item details may be in variables.docx, which was not retrieved.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same parent project of adolescent AI chatbot dependency as "Paper 1" and a separate companion OSF registration on mindful use and escapism. Later results articles from this project, using the same sample, should be checked as possible eligible reports.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (protocol) with no results. It plans to measure loneliness (Hughes et al. short scale), escapism and mindful technology use, and says it will report zero-order correlations at Stage 0, but no values are given. Excluded under E5 (protocol without results). Search for the later results paper.

codes.sample: Planned: at least 128 Indonesian university students (64 per motivation condition), recruited by purposive sampling through social media for lab sessions. No data reported.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI assistant used in a lab task (an AI system set up by the researchers for Excel tasks)
codes.dependence_measures: Generative AI Dependency Scale (Goh et al., 2025): 9 items adapted into Indonesian, 3 per dimension, 5-point Likert. Behavioural measure: cosine similarity between participants' prompts and the task instructions. Post-task quiz as a supplementary measure.
codes.possible_duplicate: Any later results paper from this OSF preregistration (dgnvm) would describe the same planned sample.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (a protocol) with no results: data collection had not been analysed when it was registered. The only planned correlations are between GAID and cosine similarity (convergent validity) and between Excel Skill and GAID (assumption check). Excel Skill is a task-specific skill covariate, not general or academic self-efficacy. Check for a later results report.

codes.sample: Planned: school students aged 12–18 years in Beijing and Inner Mongolia (expected N 1,200–1,600: 700–900 Beijing, 500–700 Inner Mongolia), T1 of a three-wave cohort; online survey, data collection 10–20 Oct 2026. No data reported.
codes.ai_system: AI tools in general (AI use / AI dependency among adolescents; no specific system named)
codes.dependence_measures: 12-item AI-dependency measure rated 1–6: instrumental AI dependency (ID, items 1–6) and relational/emotional AI dependency (RD, items 7–12; item 11 reverse-scored). Planned correlates: WHO-5 well-being, single-item loneliness, PHQ-4 psychological distress.
codes.possible_duplicate: The registration says "All four studies use the same T1 sample" (a shared three-wave adolescent cohort in Beijing/Inner Mongolia, ethics approvals Z2026SY016/Z2026SY017). Any later results paper or sibling OSF registration from this cohort would describe the same sample.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (5n7ab) without results. The authors certify they had not accessed the data, and collection was still running (10–20 Oct 2026). It measures AI dependency (ID/RD) and eligible correlates (well-being, loneliness, PHQ-4 distress) and plans to report correlations, but none are reported yet. Flag it to look for the future results paper.

codes.sample: Planned: school-enrolled adolescents aged 12–18 at baseline, convenience sample from several secondary schools in one region (China), target n≈800–1,000, three waves (T1 October 2026, ~12-month follow-up). No data collected yet.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI / LLMs (general)
codes.dependence_measures: LLM-D12 (LLM Dependence Scale): instrumental dependency (ID) and relational/emotional dependency (RD), each a 6-item mean. Planned only.
codes.possible_duplicate: Check later for a results paper from this OSF preregistration (vdz9q; Capital Medical University ethics Z2026SY016) on authenticity profiles, AI dependency and mental health in adolescents.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (protocol) with no results. It says: "Data does not yet exist" and "T1 formal data collection has not begun." Planned measures: LLM-D12 ID/RD, WHO-5, loneliness and PHQ-4, so a results paper could be eligible later. No associations are reported.

codes.sample: Planned: general-public adults 18+, recruited via Discord, subreddits, SurveyCircle, PollPool; target N=300 (minimum 150). No data reported.
codes.ai_system: AI companions and AI tools in general (users classed as non-AI-user, tool user or AI companion)
codes.dependence_measures: None named in the registration text. The AI variable is the 'Respondent Path', a 3-level grouping from a usage screener and a relationship characterization scale, which is not a dependence measure.
codes.possible_duplicate: A future results paper from this OSF project (ryb5n) may report this sample.
codes.note: OSF preregistration (protocol) with no results. Planned correlates: PHQ-9 depression, UCLA-3 loneliness. Spearman correlations are planned. No dependence/addiction measure is described in the text received. The linked survey PDF and analysis plan were not retrieved. Would also likely fail E1 if results were published.

codes.sample: Planned: adolescents aged 13-18 in England who use AI chatbots, recruited through schools (target 800 analysable participants across ≥15 schools). No results reported.
codes.ai_system: AI chatbots in general (participant's primary chatbot), with a randomised school/work or non-school/private use-context prompt
codes.dependence_measures: Planned: AI chatbot dependency, Goh et al. (2025) Generative AI Dependency scale, 11 items, 5-point, context-anchored mean total score
codes.possible_duplicate: Same parent project and sample as a companion OSF registration/paper (the 'companion predictors paper', a multilevel predictor-mapping study). Any results paper from this registration, or from the companion one, may report the same sample.
codes.note: OSF registration only, filed before analysis. It has no data or results, so it counts as a protocol without results. It plans to report zero-order correlations between AI dependency and mindful technology use (mindfulness), escapism and loneliness (3-item UCLA), plus single-predictor models. The results papers should be tracked down and screened.

codes.sample: Planned: about 400 adult Prolific participants, English-fluent, in a 3x2 between-subjects experiment. Per the registration, data collection had not started: "Data does not yet exist."
codes.ai_system: AI writing assistant presented as ChatGPT (familiar) or AI-Bot (unfamiliar); also general AI use
codes.dependence_measures: AI Dependency Scale (ADS), mean score, alpha = .75, planned as a continuous predictor. Over-reliance is also planned as observed task behaviour (Levenshtein distance, lie detection).
codes.possible_duplicate: Study 2a of the same dissertation as Study 1: Frenkenberg & Hochman (2025), "It's Scary to Use It, It's Scary to Refuse It", Systems 13, 82. Study 1 measured AI dependency and AI anxiety (fear of AI) and reported correlations, so it should be screened separately.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration (protocol) with no data or results. The planned analyses are only multivariable regressions. No zero-order associations are reported. The only planned eligible correlate is AI-related anxiety (AI Anxiety Scale). Check for a later results paper for Study 2a.

codes.sample: Planned: about 200 undergraduate students at the University of Erfurt (ErfurtLab), possibly also from other universities. Online LimeSurvey data collection planned for 20 March – 4 May 2026. "Data does not yet exist."
codes.ai_system: Generative AI (genAI) in general
codes.dependence_measures: Planned measures of functional dependence and existential/emotional dependence on genAI. No items or scale are described. The plan says "All remaining items will be analyzed individually and will not be aggregated into scales."
codes.possible_duplicate: A later results paper or thesis from this registered study (OSF dvsm3, University of Erfurt) may exist and should be checked separately.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration with no results ("Data does not yet exist"), so it is a protocol without results (E5). Even with results, the planned variables include no eligible correlate: they are decision competence, cognitive reflection, socioeconomic status and demographics. no_eligible_correlate would also apply.

codes.sample: Planned: adolescents aged 12–18 years in Beijing and Inner Mongolia. Expected N is about 1,200–1,600 (about 1,500). AI-dependency models will use only students who used generative AI in the past month. Data collection is planned for 10–20 October 2026. No data were collected or analysed at the time of registration.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI (in general)
codes.dependence_measures: A 12-item AI-dependency scale rated 1–6: 6 items on instrumental AI dependency (ID) and 6 items on relational/emotional AI dependency (RD), with item 11 reverse-scored. The scale is described in the plan, but no data or results are reported.
codes.possible_duplicate: Shared three-wave adolescent cohort (Beijing/Inner Mongolia). The registration states: "All four studies use the same T1 sample." Other OSF preregistrations or later articles from this cohort that report ID/RD with PHQ-4, WHO-5 or loneliness would describe the same sample.
codes.note: This is an OSF preregistration with no results: "the authors certify that they have not accessed any of that data." Eligible correlates are planned (PHQ-4 psychological distress, WHO-5 well-being, and a single loneliness item), and the plan says correlations will be reported. Any results paper from this cohort should be checked for eligibility.

codes.sample: University students in higher education (no sample size or other details in the registration text).
codes.ai_system: Generative AI (general)
codes.dependence_measures: Functional and emotional AI dependence. The registration names these but does not give the instrument.
codes.possible_duplicate: This could be the registration for a later or parallel article with the same title. Check whether that article exists and whether it has already been screened.
codes.note: OSF registration w59r6, filed after data collection. It gives only hypotheses and the analysis plan, with no results, so it counts as a protocol without results. The planned correlates (academic self-efficacy, mindfulness facets) are eligible. The published article, if found, would probably be eligible because a correlation analysis is planned.

codes.sample: Planned only: 1,200–1,600 school students aged 12–18 in Beijing (700–900) and Inner Mongolia (500–700). Convenience sample from the T1 wave of a three-wave cohort. AI-dependency models will use only students who used generative AI in the past month. No data are reported.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI (general)
codes.dependence_measures: A planned 12-item AI-dependency scale rated 1–6, with two subscales: instrumental AI dependency (ID, items 1–6) and relational/emotional AI dependency (RD, items 7–12; item 11 reverse-scored).
codes.possible_duplicate: The registration says "All four studies use the same T1 sample" from a shared three-wave cohort in Beijing and Inner Mongolia (ethics approvals Z2026SY016 and Z2026SY017). Any results papers or sister OSF registrations from this cohort will share the same sample.
codes.note: OSF preregistration with no results. Data collection runs 10–20 Oct 2026; data will be frozen 21 Oct 2026. Eligible correlates are planned (PHQ-4 distress, WHO-5 well-being, a single loneliness item), but the planned analyses are LPA and BCH models, not zero-order correlations. Watch for a later results report.

codes.sample: Planned only: target N = 530 adult (18+) English-speaking users of LLM-based chatbots, recruited online. "Data does not yet exist."
codes.ai_system: LLM-based chatbots / AI chatbots in general
codes.dependence_measures: Planned: dependence-related AI chatbot use measured with an adapted Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale and the LLM-D12 (LLM Dependence Scale). No data collected yet.
codes.possible_duplicate: Look for a later results paper or preprint from this OSF preregistration (2jxw5, registered 2026-03-22) that may report the planned correlations.
codes.note: This is a preregistration with no results ("No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists"). It plans to measure psychological distress (BSI-18), well-being (WHO-5), loneliness (UCLA) and escapism, all eligible correlates, but reports no data. If a results report comes out later, screen it separately.

codes.sample: Planned: school-enrolled Chinese adolescents aged 12–18, target baseline 800–1,000 (convenience sample from several secondary schools in one region). Three waves about 5–6 months apart, T1 planned for October 2026. Primary analysis restricted to consistent generative-AI users. No data collected yet.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI / LLMs in general
codes.dependence_measures: LLM-D12 (LLM Dependence Scale), scored as two separate six-item subscale means: instrumental dependency (ID) and relational/emotional dependency (RD). No total score is calculated.
codes.possible_duplicate: This is the OSF preregistration (9y73g) of a planned three-wave RI-CLPM study. Any later results article from the Capital Medical University cohort (ethics Z2026SY017) would report this sample and should be screened on its own.
codes.note: Preregistration or protocol with no results. The text says "Data does not yet exist" and "T1 formal data collection has not begun". Planned correlates that would be eligible: PHQ-4 psychological distress (anxiety and depression), WHO-5 well-being, and loneliness. Not eligible now (E5_design), but a later results paper could be.

codes.sample: Planned: Chinese middle school and university students aged 10-24 from four sites (Longzhou, Yancheng, Zhenjiang, Tanshan). 10,750 questionnaires collected; N = 3,885 after data cleaning. Cross-sectional, data collected 2023 to June 2025.
codes.ai_system: AI in general ("AI use"; the purposes of AI use in the past year), measured with the AIMEU22 scale
codes.dependence_measures: AIMEU22 scale: its problematic AI use factor (total score of problematic AI use) plus motivational and perceived-impact factors. No item content or scores are reported.
codes.possible_duplicate: This preregistration probably belongs to a later AIMEU22 validation or network-analysis article from the same group (N = 3,885 Chinese students). If that article is found, check it separately.
codes.note: OSF preregistration (retrospective, 344-4) with no results: no correlations or tables. It measured only demographics, AI-use motivations, problematic AI use and perceived impact (344-62), so it would also fail as no_eligible_correlate. Planned analyses are networks, Bayesian paths and multiple regression.

codes.sample: Planned: students aged 12–18 years in Beijing (expected 700–900) and Inner Mongolia (expected 500–700), 1,200–1,600 in total. AI-dependency models are limited to people who used generative AI in the past month. Data collection was scheduled for 10–20 Oct 2026, and no results are reported.
codes.ai_system: Generative AI in general
codes.dependence_measures: A 12-item AI-dependency scale scored 1–6, with two 6-item dimensions: instrumental AI dependency (ID) and relational/emotional AI dependency (RD). Item 11 is reverse-scored.
codes.possible_duplicate: The text says "All four studies use the same T1 sample" from a shared Beijing/Inner Mongolia adolescent cohort (ethics approvals Z2026SY016 and Z2026SY017). Any later results papers from this cohort may overlap in sample.
codes.note: OSF preregistration (registered 2026-10-10) with no results, i.e. a protocol without data. Relevant measures are planned: ID/RD AI dependency, WHO-5, single-item loneliness and PHQ-4. The planned analyses are LPA, three-step and BCH models, with no zero-order correlations promised. Check later for a results paper.

codes.sample: Planned purposive sample of active Indonesian undergraduates (political science, communication or related social sciences) who use generative AI. No actual sample is reported: "[Catatan: komposisi dan jumlah subjek penelitian harus ditentukan berdasarkan data penelitian asli...]"
codes.ai_system: Generative AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity) used as a source of political information
codes.dependence_measures: None. 'Political Dependency terhadap AI' (PDAI) is put forward as a conceptual or interpretive framework, studied through semi-structured interviews, observation and documentation. The authors note that it still needs to be operationalised in future work.
codes.note: Qualitative case study and theoretical synthesis. The Results section is placeholder text: "Bagian Hasil berikut ini bersifat ilustratif... HARUS diganti dengan data penelitian asli". It has no quantitative dependence measure, no correlates and no data. "Dependency" here means epistemic or political reliance, another sense of the term (E3 also applies).

codes.sample: 497 university students, cross-sectional online survey (from OSF registration description); country and demographics not stated in retrieved text.
codes.ai_system: AI in general (university students' AI use; specific tools not stated in retrieved text)
codes.dependence_measures: "AI dependency" and "AI attachment" were assessed. The retrieved text does not name the instruments, so it is unclear whether they are multi-item dependence scales.
codes.possible_duplicate: OSF registration x9wvq with dataset attached. A journal article or preprint of this study probably exists. Check against other records on distress, AI attachment and AI dependency in students (n=497).
codes.note: Only the OSF registration form was retrieved; it has no results. It reports that psychological distress and AI dependency were measured and analysed with Pearson correlations, so the study is probably eligible. A reviewer needs the full article or the .sav dataset (osf.io/download/6aa69b40bfc17233a5b2fb67) to get r and identify the instruments.
